# Issues and GitHub Projects {#sec-projects}

The backlog moves out of `TODO.md` and onto a board in GitHub Projects, where every task has an owner, a status, a history, and the PR that resolved it.

A `TODO.md` works while you're alone. With two people, it doesn't show who is doing what, doesn't allow discussion per item, and causes merge conflicts when both edit it at once.

## Item types

- **Issue:** a real task, with a description, discussion, and links to PRs. It's the unit of work.
- **Draft item:** an idea jotted straight onto the board, without becoming an issue. Use it to capture things fast; convert it to an issue when you start working on it.
- **Pull request:** appears on the board and moves on its own as it's reviewed and merged.

## The life cycle of an item

```{mermaid}
stateDiagram-v2
    direction TB
    [*] --> Backlog: item created
    Backlog --> Next: picked in planning
    Next --> InProgress: someone took it
    InProgress --> InReview: PR opened
    InReview --> InProgress: changes requested
    InReview --> Done: PR merged
    Done --> [*]
    InProgress: In progress
    InReview: In review
```

Three transitions can be automatic: item created, PR opened, and PR merged. The rest are people's decisions.

## The three views

Projects shows the same items in three ways:

| View | What it's for | When to use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Board (Kanban) | See the flow and drag cards | Day to day |
| Table | Sort, filter, bulk-edit fields | Triage and planning |
| Roadmap | Items on a timeline | Conversations about dates |

## Recommended setup

**Fields:**

- **Status:** Backlog, Next, In progress, In review, Done.
- **Priority:** P0 to P3 (table below).
- **Area:** at Farol, `api`, `web`, `admin`, `ops`, `docs`.
- **Estimate:** 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 (Chapter [-@sec-agile]).
- **Iteration:** two-week cycles (Chapter [-@sec-agile]).

**Labels in the repository:** `bug`, `feature`, `ops`, `security`, `debt`, `docs`, `good first issue`.

**Built-in automations** (the project's Workflows menu):

- Item added to the project → Status = Backlog.
- PR opened → Status = In review.
- Issue or PR closed → Status = Done.

## Priorities in plain language

| Priority | Means | Farol example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | Production broken or data at risk: drop everything | Users can't log in |
| P1 | Blocks the iteration's goal | The aggregator import is failing |
| P2 | Important, goes into the next iterations | A new annual report |
| P3 | Nice to have | A visual tweak to a chart |

## What makes a good issue

A good issue answers three questions:

1. **What is the problem** or need?
2. **What is the expected outcome?**
3. **How do we know it's done?** (acceptance criteria)

```markdown
## Problem
Users can't export the annual report as a PDF.

## Expected outcome
An "Export PDF" button on the annual report screen.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The PDF has the same rows as the screen
- [ ] Amounts in BRL and USD are formatted
- [ ] It works for a user with more than one space
```

## Habits that make the board work

- **Every code change starts from an issue**, and the PR says `Closes #123`. That way the issue closes on its own at merge.
- **Nobody has more than two things "In progress"** at the same time. Work started and then parked is the most common waste.
- **Loose ideas go in as drafts** in the Backlog, without ceremony.
- **The Backlog gets pruned** at every planning session: anything nobody will do in the next three months is closed with a comment.

::: {.callout-tip title="In this repository"}
Each chapter of the book is an issue on the [project board](https://github.com/Garon-Sys/saas-handbook/projects). The fields, views, and automations are exactly the ones in this chapter. The script [`scripts/bootstrap-issues.sh`](https://github.com/Garon-Sys/saas-handbook/blob/main/scripts/bootstrap-issues.sh) creates the labels and the initial issues.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Try it"}
Take five lines from your `TODO.md` and rewrite each one as problem, expected outcome, and acceptance criteria. If one doesn't fit, maybe it's an idea (a draft), not a task.
:::
